newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexican general arrested on drugs charges.
newsitem.headline: Mexican general arrested on drugs charges.

text.p: Mexican authorities on Monday arrested an army brigadier general on charges of offering to bribe a top anti-drugs official $1 million a month to turn a blind eye to drug shipments, the attorney general's office said.

In a statement, the attorney general's office said the brigadier general, Alfredo Navarro Lara, "offered $1 million a month in the name of the 'Arellano Felix' brothers criminal organization to the delegate of the attorney general's office in the state of Baja California to allow the entrance and exit of drugs."

It said Navarro Lara threatened the lives of the delegate, Jose Luis Chavez Garcia and his family if he turned down the offer. The Arellano Felix brothers are leaders of one of Mexico's most powerful cocaine cartels.
After his arrest, in which members of the Defense Ministry took part, Navarro Lara was jailed in Mexico's highest security prison, Almoloya de Juarez, just outside Mexico City.

His capture marked the second arrest of a top Mexican general on drugs corruption charges in just over a month. In February, Gen. Jesus Gutierrez Rebollo, the head of Mexico's main anti-drugs unit was jailed, in a case that threw a cloud over joint Mexico-U.S. anti-narcotics efforts.
